correspondence.component_scope: Opening east of Gouin and the marsh/pond sequence northwest of Rivas
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is east of Gouin in the San Juan/Santa Rosa rural setting and trends south and southwest across low marsh and pond terrain toward the broad wet area northwest of Rivas. The original 250k and 50k views depict scattered headward ponds, parcel/road crossings and extensive marsh. They do not establish a continuous selected feeder from the headward ponds into the lower drainage through the whole interval.
correspondence.correspondence: Material pending. This concerns an extended headward wetland connection, not an exact spring-tip or bank-position match. No hydronym is assigned to the unsupported opening.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Natural marshes and scattered ponds; no reservoir or dam identified in the inspected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower headwater drainage west and south of Rivas, north of Suipacha
correspondence.finding: South of the unresolved opening, the original 250k map depicts the drainage running southeast past the Los Leones and El Carmen rural settings, turning east/northeast north of Suipacha. The southern Arroyo del Durazno approach is mapped at the lower confluence area, and the continuing trunk is labeled Río Luján. ComiLu separately states that Del Durazno and Los Leones give rise to the Río Luján at Suipacha. That prose establishes the named headwater relationship, not the missing far-upstream connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the visible lower drainage and Durazno–Luján confluence setting at ordinary corridor scale. Los Leones is bounded prose-supported headwater context; no exact name-transition vertex or automatic propagation into the entire northern opening.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Broad natural wetland drainage. The narrow white strip in one detail rendering is not evidence; the earlier original overview covers that portion.

correspondence.component_scope: Mercedes, Olivera, Villa Flandria and Luján middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected channel proceeds northeast to the Mercedes area, skirts the northern city, bends east through the Olivera and Villa Flandria corridor and continues to Luján. The original mapping shows the trunk and converging tributary valleys, including the Moyano approach upstream of Mercedes. ComiLu independently names Mercedes and Luján among its river sampling localities.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the complete middle corridor, bends and material tributary convergence settings. Nearby tributaries retain their own identities.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: A river and floodplain/wetland corridor; no material reservoir crossing identified.

correspondence.component_scope: Luján to the Pilar/Manzanares area and north to Estación Río Luján
correspondence.finding: From Luján the selected stream turns northeast through the Open Door/Manzanares setting, passes north of Pilar, then follows the lowland river north through the Zelaya and Los Cardales vicinity to the Estación Río Luján/transport crossing area. The original shows the connected trunk, floodplain and tributary junction settings across this interval.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at generalized river-corridor scale up to the reserve-side departure. Source labels do not name every neighboring stream Luján.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Lowland floodplain and marshes; the reserve wetland complex becomes material farther downstream.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northward Otamendi reserve passage to Vuelta del Tordillo
correspondence.finding: After the river reaches the Estación Río Luján vicinity, the selected trace turns north through the reserve interior near Laguna Grande and toward the Paraná bend at Vuelta del Tordillo. Original IGN mapping and APN base/hydrographic/zoning maps distinguish Laguna Grande, the western Camino Islas Malvinas corridor with canals, and Canal Santa María east of the lagoon. The province article confirms that Santa María links Luján and Paraná de las Palmas, but that general relationship does not identify this selected, more westerly passage. The inspected maps do not establish the complete selected link from Luján through the lagoon-side interior to the western Paraná junction.
correspondence.correspondence: Material pending. Canal Santa María is an independently mapped adjacent connector and is not assigned to the selected passage. The reserve and lagoon observations establish setting only; they do not supply missing connectivity.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Grande and neighboring Laguna del Pescado are natural accumulation wetlands in the APN account. Their hydronyms are not propagated to the selected line. No reservoir inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Paraná de las Palmas downstream reach and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: From the Vuelta del Tordillo area the selected downstream course follows the large mapped Paraná de las Palmas southeast, past Puerto Paraná/Boca Carabelas and the downstream channel junctions, including the Canal Gobernador Arias setting. It reaches the broad channel near the Rec. Yacaré/Isla Nueva setting. The retained endpoint is within this mapped Paraná de las Palmas channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the downstream selected receiving-channel reach and actual terminal setting. This does not establish the preceding unresolved Otamendi connector or convert this reach into Río Luján.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Delta channels and islands. A separate Luján sea mouth is not established at the selected endpoint; the retained sea class remains model metadata.

correspondence.component_scope: Opening north of I-4, Sand Lake and wetland approach to Lake Lowery
correspondence.finding: The opening lies by the Deen Still Road/Ronald Reagan Parkway wetlands, west of the US 27 corridor. The selected line crosses I-4, follows the Sand Lake and wetland/pond complex, then approaches Lake Lowery from the north. The original overview and more detailed opening view show local channels, wooded wetlands, ponds and the highway, but do not establish the entire selected through-waterway. Continuous wetland cover alone does not resolve the connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Lowery and conditional southern outlets
correspondence.finding: USGSTopo places the selected lake crossing and southwestern continuation toward Lake Haines. The 2017 report, printed pp.9–12 and Appendix A pp.3–5, independently maps high-water southern outlets toward the Peace basin, including the Haines side; Lowery primarily drains north. These conditional outlet links are established at corridor scale, without inferring continuous southward flow or operation of any structure today.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Haines-side transfer, Lake Fannie and Lake Hamilton
correspondence.finding: USGSTopo and the report show the connected northern lake-chain setting. The mapped Haines connection runs via the Rochelle–Conine–Smart side; the selected line instead transfers southeast east of Rochelle toward Fannie. The sources do not establish that selected direct transfer. Fannie’s eastward canal to Hamilton and the selected Hamilton lake passage are mapped and read. Lake Henry and the Middle/Little Lake Hamilton arms remain contextual branches.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Hamilton outlet and Peace Creek canal southward
correspondence.finding: The original map depicts the Hamilton outlet and the drainage-canal corridor south along the Dundee/Waverly side of Winter Haven. The selected generalized route follows this canal/wetland complex toward the Lake Wales side. Nearby Lake Annie, Ashton, Starr and Parker are distinguished and are not all treated as selected lake passages.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Peace Creek westward wetland reach, Lake Garfield and return toward Bartow
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns west through the wetland/canal complex, enters Lake Garfield and turns northwest toward the main Peace Creek corridor. The original detailed view maps the principal Peace Creek route north of Garfield and the Boggy Branch lake link. It does not establish the full selected approach through the intervening wetlands into Garfield and west/northwest return. The lake’s presence and its tributary connection do not alone establish the selected through-route.
correspondence.correspondence: Material selected through-connection remains unestablished; original terrain setting was read.

correspondence.component_scope: Saddle Creek junction and upper Peace River past Bartow and Fort Meade
correspondence.finding: The original map shows Peace Creek meeting Saddle Creek northeast of Bartow, with Lake Hancock upstream on the separate Saddle Creek branch. The selected downstream corridor corresponds to Peace River past Bartow, Homeland and Fort Meade; Bowlegs Creek and Whidden Creek join from distinct branches. Primary district prose independently defines the Peace River at the Saddle Creek–Peace Creek junction.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Bowling Green, Wauchula and middle Peace River
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the mapped Peace River east of Bowling Green and Wauchula and then through its broad meandering wooded valley. Payne Creek, Little Payne Creek, Hog Branch, Lake Dale Branch, Thompson Branch, Alligator Branch and Hickory Creek are distinguishable tributary/junction settings. None is renamed as the representative river.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Charlie Creek junction and Arcadia corridor
correspondence.finding: Original cartography shows the Peace River continuation through the Charlie Creek junction, south past Brownville and Arcadia, and through the Joshua Creek junction near Nocatee. Limestone Creek and other lateral channels remain separate. The entire selected intermediate corridor was read, not inferred from town or basin labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Peace River, Horse Creek and actual estuarine endpoint
correspondence.finding: The map follows the selected lower Peace corridor through the Horse Creek junction, Hull/Fort Ogden surroundings, tidal branches and islands, Harbour Heights and the Shell Creek junction. The selected endpoint lies in the Peace/Shell Creek estuarine setting by Cleveland and Long Island, east/upstream of the I-75 crossing. The wider Peace estuary continues southwest toward Punta Gorda and Charlotte Harbor beyond the selected end. No exact shoreline vertex agreement is required.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: southern headward component
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and its initial northwestward approach were located from retained model orientation only.
correspondence.correspondence: material source/connector evidence pending
correspondence.limits: The natural headward waterbody, small feeder and opening connection have no acquired original-map correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: upper northward corridor
correspondence.finding: The retained selection turns north through the southern Armark Lake map area.
correspondence.correspondence: material source/connector evidence pending
correspondence.limits: No original map establishes the selected lake/wetland passages, inlet/outlet links or side-stream junctions. Armark Lake is a sheet title here, not an identified selected through-lake.

correspondence.component_scope: middle bends and sheet transition
correspondence.finding: The retained selection proceeds through several east-west bends before crossing into the Ogden Bay map area.
correspondence.correspondence: material source/connector evidence pending
correspondence.limits: The actual hydrographic joining sequence and material junctions remain unobserved. Model continuity is not independent evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: lower inland corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues broadly north through the Ogden Bay map area toward the coast.
correspondence.correspondence: material source/connector evidence pending
correspondence.limits: No primary original maps establish the complete lower route, lake links or relationship to the named regional Pitok and Armark rivers.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal approach and actual coastal branch
correspondence.finding: The retained selection turns northwest into its modeled sea terminal. Primary ARC403 prose describes neighboring named rivers and bays at regional scale.
correspondence.correspondence: material source/connector evidence pending
correspondence.limits: The selected coastal branch and actual receiving setting have no original-map correspondence; they are not equated to the prose Pitok mouth or a neighboring outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern opening and westward hook
correspondence.finding: The original head map shows a north-northeast-running head branch connected to the upper drainage. The selected outer tip approaches that branch from the east rather than following the depicted extension. Its geographic and drainage interpretation is not resolved by the hydrography-only map. A missing hydronym alone would not create a gap; the unresolved matter is the actual opening corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Material opening interpretation remains pending.

correspondence.component_scope: Unnamed southern upper approach
correspondence.finding: South of the opening, the selected course follows the mapped southward then southwestward upper drainage past repeated eastern side-arm junctions. The original detailed view shows the westward bend, paired local channels and their convergence toward the Profeta joining setting. Local model offsets among these mapped channels are read only at generalized corridor scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Generalized upper corridor and its mapped local junctions supported; no independent hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper joining setting and northward Profeta corridor
correspondence.finding: The westward upper approach joins the mapped branch labeled Quebrada del Profeta from the south. The selected route then turns north-northwest, following repeated Profeta labels and mapped side-channel joining settings through its long middle section. The ODEPA original regional map corroborates the broader Profeta course south of Salar de Navidad, without resolving detailed tributaries.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported named middle/lower corridor and principal mapped junction settings.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower transition to westward parallel arm
correspondence.finding: The detailed original hydrographic map carries Profeta farther north before a westward bend. The selected line instead turns west sooner across the interval toward the southern parallel arm. COT maps surrounding unvegetated land and nearby wetland, while the independent aQuist regional map supplies coarse relief context. Neither establishes the through-link or positively identifies the entire modeled transition as one continuous drainage or a fully explained non-river connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Material connection gap; no scope-hold completion.

correspondence.component_scope: Salar approach and actual selected end
correspondence.finding: The final selected stretch skirts the southern part of a COT wetland polygon and ends within its western portion. ODEPA independently depicts and labels Salar de Navidad in this regional setting, with Profeta approaching from the southeast. The detailed hydrography also shows the separate arms reaching the western convergence. It does not prove the earlier shortcut into the southern arm. Mapped drainage continues beyond the selected end, so the model endpoint is not asserted to be the natural river terminus.
correspondence.correspondence: Generalized salar/selected-end setting supported; preceding through-link remains pending.
